free_tier.stated: Not published. What is documented is capability rather than quota: the dataset center accepts file, folder, or archive uploads and auto-extracts archives server-side; public datasets require a license field before they can be published (so publishing is a two-step publish flow, not a raw PUT). OpenDataLab is the org behind the WanJuan corpus and mirrors COCO and similar multi-hundred-GB sets, so its scale class is genuinely multi-TB on the read side.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-file cap, retention, or rate limit published

egress.terms: Free for public datasets; anonymous downloads. No egress line found. Served from Chinese CDN endpoints.

record.tooling: Same openxlab toolchain (OpenDataLab runs on the OpenXLab 浦源 docs stack): `pip install openxlab`, `openxlab dataset upload-file/-folder`. Also opendatalab/opendatalab-python-sdk (60 stars) and an OpenDataLab CLI documented at opendatalab.com/docs/developers/数据集/数据集CLI. There is no S3 API.
record.chaining: Per-dataset repos, unlimited count, free account. 50 GB-class datasets are the platform's normal unit, so N datasets x 50-200 GB.

limits.value: No per-file cap, retention, or rate limit published

record.limits_note: Unverified quota. Known: public publication requires a license to be set (a metadata gate, not a storage gate); archives are auto-extracted, so extracted size counts. No per-file cap, retention, or rate limit published.
record.reliability_note: API endpoints on opendatalab.com timed out from this network (25 s, then 30 s) while HTML pages served fine. Treat the programmatic surface as CN-network-dependent.
